QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_52

question.text: What is the regulatory status of Securities Transaction Tax (STT) across different derivative segments in India?

answer.text: STT is levied only on equity derivatives (futures and options); currency derivatives and interest rate derivatives are currently not subject to STT
STT applies uniformly across all exchange-traded derivatives including equity, currency, and interest rate segments
STT applies to equity and currency derivatives but not to interest rate derivatives due to their government security linkage
No derivative transactions attract STT — it applies only to cash market equity transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: STT is levied only on equity derivative transactions. Currency futures/options and interest rate futures/options are currently not subject to STT. For equity derivatives, the current workbook rates are: sale of futures at 0.02% on the seller, sale of an option at 0.10% on the seller on the option premium and exercised option at 0.125% on the purchaser on the settlement price. The Trap: STT is not universal across all derivative segments — only equity derivatives are taxed. The currency and interest-rate STT exemption is a segment-level feature, not a product-by-product exception. Derivatives ARE subject to STT in equity, so the "no derivatives attract STT" option is wrong. Note: The STT differential across segments materially affects total trading costs and can influence the choice of hedging instrument. Combine STT with stamp duty (applicable to all segments at varying rates) and GST for the full cost picture.
